questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A man owned a large tract of land. During his lifetime, the man conveyed the easterly half to his son and the westerly half to his daughter. Both of the conveyances, which were promptly and properly recorded, contained the following language: "The parties agree for themselves and their heirs and assigns that the premises herein conveyed shall be used only for residential purposes; that each lot created within the premises herein conveyed shall contain not less than five acres; and that each lot shall have not more than one single-family dwelling. This agreement shall bind all successor owners of all or any portion of the premises and any owner of any part of the premises may enforce this covenant."
After the man's death, the son decided to build houses on half-acre lots in the easterly tract as authorized by current applicable zoning and building codes. The area surrounding this tract was developed as a residential community with homes built on half-acre lots. The westerly tract is in a residential area covered by a different zoning code, which allows residential development only on five-acre tracts of land.
The daughter has filed an appropriate action to enjoin the son's proposed construction on half-acre lots, claiming that the proposal violates the restrictions set forth in the man's conveyance.
Is the court likely to find the restrictions in the conveyance valid?

choices.A: No, because of the change of circumstance in the neighborhood.
choices.B: No, because the restriction conflicts with the applicable zoning code.
choices.C: Yes, because the original grantees still own their respective tracts.
choices.D: Yes, because the provision imposed an equitable servitude.

questions.explanation:
Elements of real covenants & equitable servitudes

Real covenants
(enforceable by money damages)		 Equitable servitudes
(enforceable by equitable relief)
For burden to run Writing, Intent to run, Touch & concern, Horizontal & vertical privity, Notice Express: Writing, Intent to run, Touch & concern, Notice
For benefit to run Writing, Intent to run, Touch & concern, Limited vertical privity, No notice required
Implied: Intent to create common scheme, Restrictive servitude, Notice

Equitable servitudes are express or implied covenants (promises) regarding land that are enforceable in equity, usually by injunction.

Express equitable servitudes have four elements:

  • Writing: Expressed in writing satisfying the statute of frauds (e.g., deeds).
  • Intent to run: Parties intend for the covenant to bind successors (e.g., “heirs and assigns”).
  • Touch and concern: Relates to the use or occupation of both the dominant and servient estates (e.g., residential use restrictions).
  • Notice: The owner of the servient estate has actual, record, or inquiry notice of the covenant.

Here, the deed restriction satisfies all four elements of an express equitable servitude and will be enforceable against subsequent purchasers of the servient estate who had notice.

(Choice A) The “Changed Conditions Doctrine” allows termination of a servitude if circumstances in the neighborhood have changed so much that the purpose of the servitude can no longer be fulfilled. However, this doctrine applies only in extraordinary circumstances and does not apply here.

(Choice B) A covenant restricting lots to five acres does not conflict with a zoning code that authorizes lots as small as one-half acre. The restriction is more restrictive than the zoning ordinance, which is permissible; zoning sets a floor, not a ceiling.

(Choice C) A valid equitable servitude runs with the land and binds subsequent owners of the servient estate even if the original grantees no longer own their tracts, provided the successor had notice of the covenant. The fact that the original grantees still own their land is not required.

📌 Educational Objective

To create an express equitable servitude, four things are needed: (1) writing, (2) intent to run to successors, (3) touch and concern the land, and (4) notice to the servient-estate owner.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Property: Servitudes § 2.1 (2000).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子拥有一大片土地。在该男子生前，他将东半边的土地转让给了他的儿子，西半边的土地转让给了他的女儿。这两份转让文件都及时并妥善地进行了登记，其中包含以下语言："双方为自己及其继承人和受让人同意，本协议所转让的地产仅可用于住宅目的；在本协议所转让的地产内创建的每一地块面积不得少于五英亩；且每一地块上不得拥有一处以上的独户住宅。本协议应对该地产全部或任何部分的所有继任所有权人具有约束力，且该地产任何部分的所有权人均可执行此契约。"

在该男子去世后，其子决定根据现行适用的区划和建筑法规的授权，在东边地块上建造占地半英亩的房屋。该地块周边的区域已被开发为住宅区，房屋均建在半英亩的地块上。西边地块位于一个适用不同区划法规的住宅区，该法规只允许在五英亩的土地上进行住宅开发。

女儿已提起适当的诉讼，请求禁止其兄计划在半英亩地块上进行建设，声称该计划违反了男子转让文件中规定的限制。

法院是否可能认定转让文件中的限制有效？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为邻近地区情况发生了变化。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该限制与适用的区划法规相冲突。
zh-choices.C: 会的，因为最初的受让人仍拥有他们各自的地块。
zh-choices.D: 会的，因为该条款设定了一项衡平法上的地役(equitable servitude)。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Equitable Servitudes
正确答案：D

是的，因为该条款设定了一项衡平法上的地役 (Equitable Servitude)。

🔍 核心法律分析

本题的关键在于识别原告（女儿）寻求的救济方式：禁令 (Injunction)。

当一方试图通过禁令来强制执行土地使用限制时，法院会应用衡平法地役权 (Equitable Servitude) 的规则，而不是普通法上的地产契约 (Real Covenant)。

要确立一项对后续所有者有约束力的衡平法地役权，通常需要满足以下要素（WITN）：

  • Writing (书面形式)： 限制条款包含在原始的转让契据中。
  • Intent (意图)： 契据明确指出“bind all successor owners”（约束所有继任所有者）。
  • Touch and Concern (涉及并关系土地)： 限制了土地的使用方式（仅限住宅、最小5英亩），这直接影响了土地的价值和使用。
  • Notice (通知)： 契据已登记 (Recorded)，构成了推定通知 (Constructive/Record Notice)。

由于满足了所有要素，该限制作为衡平法地役权是有效的，法院可以颁布禁令。

⚖️ Real Covenant vs. Equitable Servitude

在MBE考试中，区分这两者主要看救济方式：

类型 救济方式 (Remedy)
Real Covenant
(地产契约)		 Money Damages
(金钱损害赔偿)
Equitable Servitude
(衡平法地役)		 Injunction
(禁令/强制执行)

本题中女儿要求“enjoin”（禁止）儿子的建设，因此适用 Equitable Servitude 的规则。

❌ 为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 A (Changed Conditions)：
虽然周边变成了半英亩社区，但“情势变更原则”要求变化必须如此剧烈，以至于整个地役权的目的完全落空。这里，女儿的土地仍处于5英亩区划内，她仍然能从限制儿子土地密度中获益（保持低密度环境）。只要该限制对受益地仍有价值，法院通常不会废除它。

选项 B (Zoning Conflict)：
这是一个经典的 MBE 陷阱。区划 (Zoning) 设定的是底线，而不是上限。 私人契约可以比区划法规更严格。区划允许半英亩，并不意味着禁止私人约定五英亩。两者不冲突，更严格的私人限制依然有效。

选项 C (Original Grantees)：
虽然他们确实是原始受让人，但这并不是限制有效的法律依据。限制之所以有效，是因为它满足了随土地转移 (run with the land) 的法律要素。如果仅仅因为是原始受让人，那么该限制可能被视为个人合同，无法约束未来的买家。

💡 MBE 提分技巧：
看到题目中出现“Zoning allows X, but Deed restricts to Y”（区划允许X，但契据限制为Y）时，记住黄金法则：私人契约可以比公法（区划）更严格。只要不违反公共政策（如种族歧视），更严格的私人限制通常会胜过宽松的区划法规。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A man purchased a large tract of land that consisted entirely of timberland. In order to take full advantage of the commercial value of his land, the man entered into a written agreement with a timber company. That agreement gave the timber company the right to enter the man's land to harvest as much timber as it wished, at its fair market value, for the next five years. The agreement was promptly and properly recorded.
The timber company's right to harvest timber on the man's land was not exclusive, and the man reserved the right to grant similar rights to others or to harvest timber himself.
The agreement had been in effect for just one year when the state brought a condemnation action to take the man's land for an airport.
In the condemnation action, is the timber company entitled to compensation?

choices.A: No, because the agreement between the man and the timber company created only a license.
choices.B: No, because the timber company's right to harvest timber on the man's land was not exclusive.
choices.C: Yes, because the agreement between the man and the timber company created a profit à prendre.
choices.D: Yes, because the timber company paid value for the right to harvest timber on the man's land.

questions.explanation:
Licenses, easements & profits
License Revocable privilege to enter & use another's land for specific purpose
Easement Nonpossessory interest in land that gives easement holder right to:
use another's land for specific purpose (ie, affirmative easement) or
prohibit other owner from doing something on land that owner would otherwise be allowed to do (ie, negative easement)
Profit Nonpossessory interest in land that gives profit holder right to enter another's land to remove products of soil (eg, timber, minerals, oil)

A profit à prendre—also called simply a profit—is a nonpossessory interest in land that gives the profit holder the right to enter another's land to remove specific natural resources (eg, timber). Because a profit is an interest in land, the profit holder (eg, timber company) is entitled to compensation if the government condemns the property under the power of eminent domain. This is true regardless of whether the profit holder paid value or has an exclusive right to remove the resources (Choices B & D).

(Choice A) Unlike easements and profits, licenses do not create an interest in the land. As a result, a licensee is not entitled to compensation in a condemnation action. But here, the timber company had a profit—not a license.

📌 Educational Objective

Educational objective: A profit à prendre is a nonpossessory interest in land that allows the profit holder to remove natural resources from another's land. This interest entitles the profit holder to compensation if the government condemns the property.

📚 References
  • Bates Sand & Gravel Co., Inc. v. Commonwealth, 404 N.E.2d 81, 82 (Mass. 1980) (finding that a profit à prendre is an interest in land entitled to compensation in a condemnation action).
  • Restatement (Third) of Property: Servitudes § 1.2(2) (Am. Law Inst. 2000) (defining profit à prendre).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子购买了一大片完全由林地组成的土地。为了充分利用其土地的商业价值，该男子与一家木材公司签订了一份书面协议。该协议授予木材公司在未来五年内进入该男子土地的权利，以公平市价采伐其希望采伐的任意数量的木材。该协议被及时并适当地进行了登记。

木材公司在该男子土地上采伐木材的权利并非排他性的，该男子保留了将类似权利授予他人或自己采伐木材的权利。

该协议仅生效一年，州政府就提起了征收诉讼，以征用该男子的土地建造机场。

在该征收诉讼中，木材公司是否有权获得补偿？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为该男子与木材公司之间的协议仅创设了一项许可（license）。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为木材公司在该男子土地上采伐木材的权利并非排他性的。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为该男子与木材公司之间的协议创设了一项取益权（profit à prendre）。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为木材公司为获得在该男子土地上采伐木材的权利支付了对价。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Rights in Land

✅ 正确答案：C

是的，因为该男子与木材公司之间的协议创设了一项取益权 (Profit à Prendre)。

由于取益权属于一种土地权益 (Interest in Land)，当政府行使征收权 (Eminent Domain) 时，权益持有人有权获得补偿。

⚖️ 核心考点：取益权 (Profit à Prendre)

本题的关键在于识别木材公司拥有的权利性质。

定义： 取益权是一种非占有性的土地权益 (Nonpossessory interest)，赋予持有人进入他人土地并取走土壤产物（如木材、矿产、石油、鱼类或野味）的权利。

法律逻辑推演：

  1. 识别权利：协议允许公司进入土地并“采伐木材”(harvest timber)。这符合取益权的定义。
  2. 权益性质：取益权不仅仅是合同权利，它被视为一种不动产权益 (Property Interest)。
  3. 宪法保护：根据美国宪法第五修正案，政府征收私有财产必须给予“公正补偿”(Just Compensation)。
  4. 结论：既然取益权是财产权益，政府征地导致该权益灭失，必须向公司支付补偿。

🔍 易混淆概念辨析

MBE常考取益权与许可 (License) 的区别，这是解题的关键。

特征 取益权 (Profit) 许可 (License)
性质 土地权益
(Interest in land)		 个人特权
(Privilege)
撤销性 通常不可随意撤销 通常可随时撤销
(Revocable)
征收补偿 ✅ 有权获得补偿 ❌ 无权获得补偿
典型例子 采矿、伐木、狩猎 电影票、晚宴邀请

🚫 干扰项分析

  • 选项 A (License)：错误。如果是 License，确实无权获得补偿。但因为涉及“取走资源”且有书面协议登记，这是 Profit，属于土地权益，而非仅仅是可撤销的 License。
  • 选项 B (Not Exclusive)：错误。取益权可以是排他的 (Exclusive) 也可以是非排他的 (Non-exclusive)。非排他性只影响权益的价值（补偿金额可能较少），但不影响权益的存在及获得补偿的资格。
  • 选项 D (Paid Value)：虽然支付对价是商业常态，但获得补偿的法律基础是“拥有土地权益”，而不是“是否支付了钱”。即使是赠与的 Profit，在征收时也有权获得补偿。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
Two adjacent, two-story, commercial buildings were owned by a landlord. The first floors of both buildings were occupied by various retail establishments. The second floors were rented to various other tenants. Access to the second floor of each building was reached by a common stairway located entirely in Building 1. While the buildings were being used in this manner, the landlord sold Building 1 to a man by warranty deed that made no mention of any rights concerning the stairway. About two years later, the landlord sold Building 2 to a woman. The stairway continued to be used by the occupants of both buildings. The stairway became unsafe as a consequence of regular wear and tear. The woman entered the man's building and began the work of repairing the stairway. The man demanded that the woman discontinue the repair work and vacate the man's building. When the woman refused, the man brought an action to enjoin the woman from continuing the work.
For which party should judgment be entered?

choices.A: The man, because the woman has no rights in the stairway.
choices.B: The man, because the woman's rights in the stairway do not extend beyond the normal life of the existing structure.
choices.C: The woman, because she has a right to take whatever action is necessary to protect herself from possible tort liability to persons using the stairway.
choices.D: The woman, because she has an easement in the stairway and an implied right to keep the stairway in repair.

questions.explanation:
Implied easements
Type Elements
Necessity
  • Severance of common ownership
  • Strict necessity for use & enjoyment of land
Existing prior use
  • Severance of common ownership
  • Prior existing use
  • Apparent & continuous
  • Reasonable necessity for use & enjoyment of land

An easement can be implied by an existing prior use when the following elements are met:

  • Severance of common ownership – the dominant and servient estates were a single tract of land, and the owner retained part of the tract and conveyed the rest to another
  • Prior existing use – the owner used the servient estate to benefit the dominant estate (ie, a “quasi-easement”)
  • Apparent and continuous – the prior use was discoverable by reasonable inspection and continued until the tract was severed
  • Reasonable necessity – continuance of the prior use is reasonably necessary to use the land

Here, the woman and the man owned a single tract as tenants in common. When the woman conveyed Building 1 to the man while retaining Building 2, common ownership was severed. Before severance, the owner used the stairway in Building 1 to access Building 2—a prior existing quasi-easement that was apparent and continuous. Continued use of the stairway is reasonably necessary for the woman to enjoy Building 2. Therefore, the woman has an implied easement in the stairway (Choice A).

As the easement holder, the woman has the sole duty to maintain* the easement. Repairs must be made to avoid harm to the servient estate and to protect the servient owner (not the easement holder) from liability for harm to third parties (Choice C). As a result, the easement holder has the implied right to enter the servient estate to make necessary repairs—as the woman did here. Judgment should therefore be entered for her.

*However, if the easement is used by the easement holder and the servient owner, then repair costs will be apportioned between the parties based on their relative use.

(Choice B) An easement over a structure (eg, building) continues until that structure is destroyed by natural causes. And since Building 2 still exists, the woman’s easement over the stairway remains in effect.

📌 Educational Objective

An easement will be implied by prior use if (1) common ownership was severed, (2) the prior existing use was apparent and continued after severance, and (3) continuation of that use is reasonably necessary to use the land.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Property: Servitudes § 2.12 (Am. Law Inst. 2000) (easement by prior use)
questions.zh-question:
一位房东拥有两栋相邻的两层商业楼。两栋楼的一楼都被各种零售商店占用，二楼则出租给其他各种租户。通往每栋楼二楼的通道是一个完全位于1号楼内的公用楼梯。在两栋楼以上述方式使用期间，房东通过一份担保契约(warranty deed)将1号楼出售给一名男子，该契约未提及任何与楼梯相关的权利。大约两年后，房东将2号楼出售给一名女子。该楼梯继续由两栋楼的住户使用。由于正常的磨损，楼梯变得不安全。该女子进入男子的楼内，开始修理楼梯。该男子要求女子停止维修工作并离开其楼宇。女子拒绝后，男子提起诉讼，请求法院下达禁令，禁止女子继续施工。

判决应有利于哪一方？

zh-choices.A: 男子，因为女子对该楼梯没有权利。
zh-choices.B: 男子，因为女子在楼梯上的权利不应超出该现有结构的正常使用寿命。
zh-choices.C: 女子，因为她有权采取任何必要行动，以保护自己免于对使用楼梯的人可能承担的侵权责任。
zh-choices.D: 女子，因为她对该楼梯拥有地役权(easement)，并享有维修楼梯的默示权利。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Implied Easements

核心考点：既有先前用途产生的默示地役权 Implied Easement by Existing Prior Use

当一块土地被分割出售时，如果之前的用途满足特定条件，法律会推定双方意图保留该用途的权利。

Building 1 (供役地 Servient)
⬅ 使用
Building 2 (需役地 Dominant)

Building 2 的住户必须通过 Building 1 的楼梯上二楼

法律规则四要素分析

本案中，法院会根据以下四个要素判定女子（Building 2 所有者）拥有地役权：

  • 所有权分割 (Severance of Title)
    两栋楼最初由同一房东拥有，后来分别卖给了男子和女子。
  • 既有先前用途 (Existing Prior Use)
    在分割前，房东一直使用该楼梯作为通往 Building 2 二楼的通道（这被称为“准地役权” Quasi-easement）。
  • 明显且持续 (Apparent and Continuous)
    楼梯的存在和使用是显而易见的，且一直持续到所有权分割之后。
  • 合理必要性 (Reasonable Necessity)
    继续使用楼梯对于 Building 2 的使用是“合理必要”的。注意：这里不需要“绝对必要” (Strict Necessity)。
维修权利 (Right to Repair)

既然女子拥有地役权，附带的法律后果是：

地役权人有权利也有义务维护地役权。

这意味着女子拥有进入供役地（Building 1）进行必要维修的默示权利 (Implied Right)。这是为了防止地役权变得无法使用，或对第三方造成危险。

选项深度解析
✅ 选项 D (正确答案)

女子拥有地役权（基于先前用途），因此享有维修楼梯的默示权利。这是最准确的法律依据。

❌ 选项 A

错误。虽然契约 (Deed) 中未提及，但地役权可以通过“默示” (Implication) 产生。

❌ 选项 B

错误。地役权的存续期通常与建筑物的存续期一致，只要建筑物还在，权利就不会因为“正常使用寿命”结束而自动终止。

❌ 选项 C

错误。虽然避免侵权责任 (Tort Liability) 是维修的动机，但它不是女子有权进入他人房产的法律依据。她能进入是因为她拥有“地役权”这一财产权利。

🎓 MBE 提分技巧

区分两种默示地役权：

  1. Implied by Prior Use: 关键词是“Common ownership” + “Prior use”。只需要 Reasonable Necessity（合理必要，比如省钱、方便）。
  2. Implied by Necessity: 通常指土地变成了“袋地” (Landlocked)。这需要 Strict Necessity（绝对必要，没有其他路可走）。

本题有楼梯作为“先前用途”，所以适用第一种标准。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A man owned a large tract of land that had frontage on a public highway. The land had no access to any other road.
Fifteen years ago, the man conveyed the rear half of the land to a woman and at the same time conveyed an express easement to the woman that provided access from her land across his retained land to the public highway.
The woman used the easement until she reconveyed the land back to the man 10 years ago. The deed to the man made no reference to the easement.
Five years ago, the man again conveyed the rear half of the land, this time to an investor in a deed that made no reference to any easement to the public highway.
Recently, the man told the investor that he could no longer cross the man's land for access to the public highway. A neighbor has told the investor that he can use her land for access to another public road "for a price."
The investor has sued the man for the right to cross the man's land to the public highway.
For whom will the court likely decide?

choices.A: The investor, because an easement will be implied.
choices.B: The investor, because the man is estopped by his grant of an easement to the woman.
choices.C: The man, because the express easement was terminated by the reconveyance.
choices.D: The man, because the investor can reasonably acquire another means of access to a public road.

questions.explanation:
Easement creation and termination

 
Man
>15 years ago
Expressly created
Man
Woman
15 years ago
Terminated by common ownership
Man
10 years ago
Implied by necessity
Man
Investor
5 years ago

The man conveyed an easement to the woman that allowed her to cross his land to access a public highway. That easement terminated when the dominant estate (woman's tract) and servient estate (man's tract) merged into the hands of one owner after the woman conveyed her tract back to the man (Choices B & C). And though the man subsequently conveyed the rear half of his lot to the investor, a terminated easement is not re-created merely by re-severing the land into two parcels.

Additionally, the investor did not receive an easement by express grant because his deed made no reference to any easement to the public highway. But an easement by necessity will be implied if two elements are met:

  • Severance of common ownership – the dominant and servient estates were a single tract of land, and the owner retained part of the tract and conveyed the rest to another
  • Strict necessity – the easement is absolutely necessary for the use and enjoyment of the land (eg, the dominant tract is landlocked and has no access to a public road)

Here, the man owned both tracts (unity of estates) before he conveyed the back half to the investor (severance). And since the rear tract has no access to a public highway or any other road, an easement over the man's tract is absolutely necessary for the investor to use and enjoy his tract. Therefore, an easement will be implied and the court will likely decide for the investor.

(Choice D) The ability to create alternative access to a landlocked parcel by purchase of an easement over a neighbor's land does not defeat the creation of an easement by necessity.

📌 Educational Objective

An easement by necessity is implied if (1) there was a unity of estates, (2) common ownership was severed, and (3) an easement is absolutely necessary to use and enjoy the land.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Property: Servitudes § 2.15 (Am. Law Inst. 2000) (easement by necessity).
  • Restatement (Third) of Property: Servitudes § 7.5 (Am. Law Inst. 2000) (termination of easement by merger).

一名男子拥有一大片临近公共高速公路的土地。该土地没有通往任何其他道路的通道。

十五年前，该男子将土地的后半部分转让给了一名女子，并同时向该女子转让了一份明示地役权（express easement），允许她从自己的土地穿过该男子保留的土地通往公共高速公路。

该女子使用了该地役权，直到十年前她将土地重新转让回该男子。转让给该男子的地契（deed）并未提及该地役权。

五年前，该男子再次将土地的后半部分转让给了一位投资者，地契中并未提及任何通往公共高速公路的地役权。

最近，该男子告诉投资者，他不能再穿过该男子的土地以通往公共高速公路。一位邻居告诉投资者，他可以付费使用她的土地以通往另一条公共道路。

投资者已起诉该男子，要求获得穿过其土地通往公共高速公路的权利。

法院可能会支持哪一方？

zh-choices.A: 支持投资者，因为将默示设定一份地役权。
zh-choices.B: 支持投资者，因为该男子因其曾向女子授予地役权而受禁止反言（estoppel）原则的约束。
zh-choices.C: 支持该男子，因为明示地役权因重新转让而终止。
zh-choices.D: 支持该男子，因为投资者可以合理地获得通往公共道路的其他途径。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Easements (地役权)
正确答案：A

支持投资者，因为将默示设定一份地役权 (Easement will be implied)。

核心法律规则：必要地役权 (Easement by Necessity)

当土地被分割导致某一部分土地成为“内陆地”（Landlocked）且无法通往公共道路时，法律会自动默示设定地役权。其构成要件为：

  • 共同所有权 (Unity of Ownership)：需役地和供役地原属于同一人。
  • 分离 (Severance)：土地被分割转让。
  • 严格必要性 (Strict Necessity)：在分割之时，除了通过供役地外，没有其他合法途径通往公共道路。
1. 旧的地役权发生了什么？(The Merger Doctrine)

虽然15年前有过明示地役权，但当女子将土地卖回给男子时，需役地和供役地归于同一人（男子）。根据混同原则 (Merger)，地役权立刻终止。当男子再次卖地给投资者时，旧的地役权不会自动复活。

2. 为什么投资者能赢？(Implied Easement)

虽然地契里没写，但法院会支持投资者，理由是必要地役权 (Easement by Necessity)：

  • 分离前：男子拥有整块地。
  • 分离后：男子卖了后半块给投资者，导致后半块地完全没有出路。
  • 必要性：为了使用这块地，投资者必须经过男子的地。
3. 邻居的提议重要吗？(Strict Necessity Analysis)

这是本题最大的干扰项（选项D）。虽然邻居说“给钱就能过”，但这不能否定“严格必要性”。

法律逻辑：必要性是看你在法律上是否有权通行。如果必须依赖第三方的许可（即使是付费），你在法律上依然是“无路可走”的。因此，不能强迫投资者去买邻居的路，他有权在原来的分割人（男子）土地上获得默示地役权。

为什么选项 B 错误？(Estoppel)
禁止反言通常需要基于当前的陈述或行为。男子给前任（女子）的地役权已经因混同而消灭，投资者不能依赖那个已经失效的权利。
为什么选项 C 错误？(Termination)
前半句是对的（明示地役权确实因混同而终止），但结论错了。旧的没了，不代表不能产生一个新的“默示”地役权。
MBE 解题技巧：
看到“Landlocked”（内陆地/无路可走）且土地源自同一前业主，优先考虑 Easement by Necessity。不要被“可以花钱买路”的选项迷惑。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A landowner granted an exclusive easement to a farmer to grow wheat for commercial use on a portion of the landowner's land for a period of 10 years. The easement made no mention of the transferability of the easement. For five years, the farmer grew wheat on the land. In year six of the easement, the farmer apportioned one-half of the easement to a rancher for grazing his cattle and the other half of the easement to a horticulturist for growing sunflowers. Unhappy with this arrangement, the landowner filed an action in court to invalidate the apportionment of the easement that he originally granted to the farmer.
Which of the following is the landowner's strongest argument that the apportionment of the easement is invalid?

choices.A: Easements that are for commercial use are not transferable.
choices.B: The burden of the easement did not automatically transfer with the land when the easement was transferred by the farmer.
choices.C: The exclusive easement was apportioned without the landowner's consent.
choices.D: The rancher and the horticulturist did not use the land in the same way as the farmer.

questions.explanation:
Distinctions between easements
Type Appurtenant
  • Benefits easement holder's land
  • Benefit & burden automatically transfer when land is conveyed
In gross
  • Benefits easement holder personally
  • Burden (not benefit) automatically transfers when land is conveyed
Purpose Affirmative Allows easement holder to do something on servient estate
Negative Restricts servient-estate owner's lawful use of servient estate
Creation Express Created by parties in writing that satisfies statute of frauds
Irrevocable license License becomes irrevocable due to estoppel or coupling with another servitude
Implied
  • Implied by law due to necessity (easement by necessity)
  • Implied by fact due to prior use (easement by implication)
By prescription Adversely acquired through OCAN—open/notorious, actual, continuous & nonpermissive use

Both an easement appurtenant and an easement in gross benefit the easement holder (ie, the owner of the dominant estate in the case of an easement appurtenant, and the holder of the easement in the case of an easement in gross). However, an easement appurtenant benefits the easement holder's land, while an easement in gross benefits the easement holder personally.

Traditionally, the benefit of an easement in gross could not be transferred, but modern courts generally hold that the benefit of an easement in gross can be transferred if the easement is for commercial use. A transferred easement in gross can also be apportioned (ie, divided up):

  • nonexclusive – cannot be divided.
  • exclusive – generally can be divided.

However, the apportionment of an exclusive easement in gross is subject to the "one stock" rule. Under this rule, the use of the easement by the transferees is limited to the use that the transferor made of the easement.

Here, the farmer's easement was for commercial use and exclusive (Choice A). Therefore, the farmer could transfer and apportion his easement. However, the landowner's strongest argument would be that the rancher and the horticulturist did not use the land in the same way as the farmer. Under the "one stock" rule, the landowner can argue that the collective use of the easement by the transferees exceeds the use that the farmer made of the easement.

(Choice B) The burden of an easement in gross automatically transfers when the burdened land is conveyed. However, this is irrelevant here because the burdened land was not transferred.

(Choice C) An exclusive easement in gross can be apportioned without the servient-estate owner's consent.

📌 Educational Objective

When an exclusive easement in gross is apportioned (ie, divided up), the "one stock" rule applies. This rule limits the collective use that the transferees can make of the easement to the use that the transferor made of the easement (ie, the transferor's "stock").

📚 References
  • Miller v. Lutheran Conference & Camp Ass'n
  • 25 Am. Jur. 2d Easements and Licenses § 79
questions.zh-question:
一名土地所有者授予一名农民一项独家地役权(exclusive easement)，允许其在该土地所有者的一部分土地上为商业用途种植小麦，为期10年。该地役权未提及可转让性。五年来，该农民一直在该土地上种植小麦。在地役权的第六年，该农民将地役权的一半分配给一个牧场主用于放牧其牛群，另一半分配给一个园艺家用于种植向日葵。土地所有者对此安排不满，向法院提起诉讼，请求宣告其最初授予农民的地役权的此次分配无效。

以下哪项是土地所有者主张地役权分配无效的最有力论点？

zh-choices.A: 用于商业用途的地役权不可转让。
zh-choices.B: 当农民转让地役权时，地役权的负担并未随土地自动转移。
zh-choices.C: 独家地役权的分配未经土地所有者同意。
zh-choices.D: 牧场主和园艺家并未以与农民相同的方式使用该土地。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Easements in Gross

核心概念：属人地役权的分配 本题考察的是Easement in Gross（属人地役权）的转让性（Transferability）与可分配性（Apportionability）。
1. 什么是属人地役权 (Easement in Gross)?

这种地役权是为了个人（或公司）的利益而设立的，而不是为了另一块土地的利益。例如：电力公司在你的土地上架设电线的权利。

  • 商业用途 (Commercial): 通常可转让。
  • 个人用途 (Personal): 传统上不可转让（除非双方另有约定）。
2. 独家性与分配 (Exclusivity & Apportionment)

如果地役权是独家的 (Exclusive)（即地役权持有人有权排除包括土地所有者在内的所有人使用），法院通常允许持有人将地役权分配 (Apportion) 给他人。

但是，有一个关键限制：

分配后的使用不得超出原授予的范围，且必须遵守 One Stock Rule（单一存量规则）。

✅ 正确答案解析 (选项 D)

论点：牧场主和园艺家并未以与农民相同的方式使用该土地。

法律依据：地役权的范围（Scope of Easement）是由授予条款严格界定的。

  • 原授予条款明确规定："to grow wheat"（种植小麦）。
  • 实际使用情况："grazing cattle"（放牧）和 "growing sunflowers"（种向日葵）。

虽然独家商业属人地役权可以分配，但受让人（牧场主和园艺家）的使用权不能超出原持有人的权利范围。放牧和种植其他作物改变了土地的使用性质，可能增加对供役地（Servient Estate）的负担（Surcharge the easement）。这是土地所有者最强有力的反驳理由。

为什么其他选项是错误的？
选项 A 错误：
用于商业用途的属人地役权（Commercial Easement in Gross）在现代法律下通常是可转让的。题目中明确是商业用途，所以不能以此为由主张无效。
选项 B 错误：
地役权的负担 (Burden) 随供役地（土地所有者的地）转移，但这与本案无关，因为土地所有者并没有卖地。本案讨论的是地役权利益 (Benefit) 的转移。
选项 C 错误：
对于独家 (Exclusive) 的属人地役权，持有人有权进行分配，通常无需土地所有者的同意。只有在非独家（Non-exclusive）的情况下，分配才可能因过度增加负担而被禁止。
💡 MBE 考试技巧 遇到地役权题目时，按以下步骤分析：
  1. 分类：是 Appurtenant 还是 In Gross？（本题是 In Gross）
  2. 性质：是 Commercial 还是 Personal？（本题是 Commercial → 可转让）
  3. 权限：是 Exclusive 还是 Non-exclusive？（本题是 Exclusive → 可分配）
  4. 范围 (Scope)：新的使用方式是否超出了原书面约定的范围？（本题的关键杀手锏）

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A franchisor who owned two adjoining parcels conveyed the eastern parcel to an entrepreneur. The franchisor covenanted in the deed to the entrepreneur that when she, the franchisor, sold the western parcel, she would impose restrictive covenants to prohibit uses that would compete with the filling station that the entrepreneur intended to construct and operate on the eastern parcel. The deed was not recorded.
The entrepreneur constructed and operated a filling station on the eastern parcel and then conveyed the eastern parcel to his station manager, who continued the filling station use. The deed did not refer to the restrictive covenant and was promptly and properly recorded.
The franchisor then conveyed the western parcel to her friend, who knew about the franchisor's covenant with the entrepreneur to impose a covenant prohibiting the filling station use but nonetheless completed the transaction when he noted that no such covenant was contained in the franchisor's deed to him. The friend began to construct a filling station on the western parcel.
The station manager brought an appropriate action to enjoin the friend from using the western parcel for filling station purposes.
If the station manager prevails, what will be the most likely reason?

choices.A: Business-related restrictive covenants are favored in the law.
choices.B: The friend had actual knowledge of the covenant to impose restrictions.
choices.C: The friend has constructive notice of the possibility of the covenant.
choices.D: The friend is bound by the covenant because of the doctrine of negative reciprocal covenants.

questions.explanation:
Elements of real covenants & equitable servitudes
Real covenants
(enforceable by money damages)		 Equitable servitudes
(enforceable by equitable relief)
For burden to run
  • Writing
  • Intent to run
  • Touch & concern
  • Horizontal & vertical privity
  • Notice

Express:

  • Writing
  • Intent to run
  • Touch & concern
  • Notice

Implied:

  • Intent to create common scheme
  • Restrictive servitude
  • Notice
For benefit to run
  • Writing
  • Intent to run
  • Touch & concern
  • Limited vertical privity
  • No notice required

Real covenants and equitable servitudes are promises regarding land use that are enforceable against successors in interest to the original parties. The key distinction between the two is the remedy sought: real covenants are enforceable by money damages, while equitable servitudes are enforceable by equitable relief (e.g., an injunction).

To enforce an express equitable servitude, the following requirements must be met:

  • Writing: The promise must satisfy the statute of frauds (e.g., contained in a deed).
  • Intent to run: The parties intended the promise to bind successors.
  • Touch and concern: The promise relates to the use or occupation of the land (e.g., a non-compete covenant for a filling station).
  • Notice: The burdened owner must have actual, record, or inquiry notice.

If the station manager prevails, it is likely because the friend had actual knowledge (notice) of the covenant.

(Choice A) Restrictive covenants are generally disfavored in the law because they interfere with the alienability of land.

(Choice C) There was no constructive (inquiry or record) notice here. No facts suggested a restriction on the land, and the deed was not recorded.

(Choice D) Negative reciprocal covenants (also called implied equitable servitudes) are implied from a common scheme of development (such as a residential subdivision), which is not present in this scenario.

📌 Educational Objective

To enforce an express equitable servitude, four elements are required: (1) writing, (2) intent to run to successors, (3) touch and concern the land, and (4) notice to the servient-estate owner.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Property: Servitudes § 5.2 (Am. Law Inst. 2000).

一名拥有两块相邻地块的特许人将东侧地块转让给了一位创业者。该特许人在授予创业者的地契中订立契约，承诺当她（特许人）出售西侧地块时，会施加限制性契约，以禁止与创业者打算在东侧地块上建造和经营的加油站相竞争的用途。该地契未被登记。

创业者在东侧地块上建造并经营了一个加油站，然后将东侧地块转让给了他的加油站经理，该经理继续经营加油站。这份地契没有提及该限制性契约，但被及时且恰当地登记了。

随后，特许人将西侧地块转让给了她的朋友。这位朋友知道特许人与创业者之间关于施加禁止加油站用途契约的约定，但当他注意到特许人给他的地契中并未包含此类契约时，仍然完成了交易。该朋友开始在西侧地块上建造一个加油站。

加油站经理提起了适当的诉讼，请求禁止该朋友将西侧地块用于加油站目的。

如果加油站经理胜诉，最可能的原因是什么？

zh-choices.A: 与商业相关的限制性契约在法律上是受到支持的。
zh-choices.B: 该朋友对施加限制的契约有实际知情。
zh-choices.C: 该朋友对契约的可能性有推定知晓。
zh-choices.D: 根据相互性消极契约原则，该朋友受该契约的约束。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析：衡平法地役权

本题考察的是不动产法中关于限制性契约（Restrictive Covenants）随土地转移的规则，特别是当原告寻求禁令（Injunction）而非金钱赔偿时。

核心区分：
如果原告寻求金钱赔偿 (Money Damages) → 适用 Real Covenant (土地物权契约) 规则。
如果原告寻求禁令 (Injunction) → 适用 Equitable Servitude (衡平法地役权) 规则。

本题中，经理（Manager）寻求的是禁止朋友（Friend）经营加油站，属于禁令，因此我们必须分析衡平法地役权的要素。

负担随土地转移的要素 (Burden to Run)

要让限制性契约的负担约束后续的土地所有者（本案中的朋友），必须满足以下条件：

  • 书面形式 (Writing)：原始契约必须是书面的（本案中特许人给创业者的地契中有写）。
  • 意图 (Intent)：当事人意图让该承诺约束继承人。
  • 涉及与关乎土地 (Touch and Concern)：限制了土地的使用方式（不许建加油站），符合此项。
  • 知情 (Notice)：这是本题的关键！后续买家在购买时必须知道该限制的存在。

为什么选项 B 是正确答案？

选项 B：该朋友对施加限制的契约有实际知情 (Actual Knowledge)。

在衡平法地役权的分析中，知情 (Notice) 是决定性的因素。知情通常分为三种：

  1. 实际知情 (Actual Notice)：买家事实上知道该限制。
  2. 推定/登记知情 (Record/Constructive Notice)：契约已在公共记录中正确登记。
  3. 调查知情 (Inquiry Notice)：土地的状况或外观理应引起买家的询问。
特许人 (F) → 创业者 (E)
(契约未登记，但有书面约定)
↓
特许人 (F) → 朋友 (Fr)
(朋友实际上知道 F 和 E 的约定)

推理逻辑：

虽然包含限制性契约的地契（特许人给创业者的）没有被登记（因此没有“登记知情”），但题目明确指出朋友在交易前“知道”（knew about）这个契约。这种实际知情 (Actual Notice) 足以让衡平法法院强制执行该地役权，禁止朋友违反约定。

其他选项为何错误？

选项 A (法律支持商业限制)：错误。
恰恰相反，法律倾向于土地的自由使用，通常不鼓励（disfavor）限制性契约。法院会严格解释此类限制。
选项 C (推定知晓 Constructive Notice)：错误。
推定知晓通常源于登记系统。题目明确说明包含契约的地契未被登记 (Deed was not recorded)。因此，朋友不可能通过查阅公报获得通知。
选项 D (相互性消极契约 Negative Reciprocal Covenants)：错误。
这个原则（也称 Common Scheme Doctrine）通常用于开发商开发大型住宅区（Subdivision）时，遗漏了某些地块的限制。本案只是两个地块的简单转让，且存在明示的契约和实际知情，不需要依赖这个默示原则。
💡 MBE 考试技巧
遇到 Real Property 的题目，首先看救济方式（赔偿 vs. 禁令）。

如果是禁令，找 Notice (知情)。即使文件未登记（Record Act 陷阱），只要买家有Actual Notice (实际知情)，他就是输家。不要被“未登记”这个事实带偏，实际知情是王牌。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A builder purchased 10 acres of undeveloped land. He intended to construct five homes, and each home was to be constructed on a two-acre lot, which was the minimum size permitted under the zoning regulations. The builder employed an architect to design the basic plan for each home, but the builder was forced to shelve those plans due to a sudden downturn in the economy.
Six years later, the builder engaged a surveyor to subdivide the land into two-acre lots. He then discovered that the local zoning board had validly rezoned the area in which the 10 acres were located a year ago, increasing the minimum lot size to two and one-half acres for new residences. The zoning ordinance does not provide for special exceptions, and the builder cannot profitably construct only four of the five homes designed by the architect.
Can the builder proceed with his plans to build five homes on two-acre lots?

choices.A: No, because the ordinance does not provide for special exceptions.
choices.B: No, because the two and one-half acre restriction properly applies to the builder's land.
choices.C: Yes, because he cannot profitably construct only four homes on the 10 acres.
choices.D: Yes, because his rights with regard to the land vested when he purchased the land.

questions.explanation:
Nonconforming use
Existing nonconformance
  • Property owner's existing use of property that conflicts with new or modified zoning law can continue until:
    • use is enlarged, changed, or abandoned or
    • if provided by zoning law, amortization period passes or use not registered
Planned nonconformance
  • Property owner's planned nonconforming use of property can proceed if right to use has vested
  • Vested right exists if, at time zoning law or modification takes effect, property owner has:
    • secured any necessary permits in good faith and
    • made substantial progress toward achieving use

When a zoning law is enacted or modified, certain properties within that zone may not conform to the new requirements. Any existing nonconforming uses are “grandfathered in,” meaning that they are allowed to continue in spite of the conflict. However, a property owner who has merely prepared for a nonconforming use when a zoning change occurs is not allowed to proceed with that use unless the property owner has a vested right in the use.

A vested right will generally be found if, at the time the zoning change takes effect, the property owner has:

  • secured any necessary permit from the proper local authority in good faith (e.g., building permit) and
  • made substantial progress toward achieving the nonconforming use (note that in a few states, securing a permit by itself is sufficient).

Here, the builder does not have a vested right in building five homes on two-acre lots because the above requirements had not been met at the time the two and one-half acre restriction took effect (Choice D). Therefore, the restriction properly applies to the builder's land, and he cannot proceed with his plans.

(Choice A) The zoning ordinance might recognize particular future uses that are permissible if a permit is obtained (i.e., a special exception permit). For example, the ordinance might explicitly require that a funeral home obtain a permit to operate its business, even in a commercially zoned area. But here, building homes on slightly smaller lot sizes is not the type of special exception that might be required to obtain a permit.*

*A property owner may seek approval for nonconforming use by requesting a variance, but the builder has not done so here.

(Choice C) The fact that the builder cannot profitably construct four homes on the 10 acres does not entitle him to build five homes on two-acre lots. However, had the zoning change eliminated any economically viable use of the land, he may have been entitled to reasonable compensation under the Fifth Amendment takings clause.

📌 Educational Objective

A property owner may proceed with plans for nonconforming use after a zoning change if the property owner has a vested right in that use. A vested right exists if, at the time a zoning change takes effect, the property owner has (1) secured any necessary permits in good faith and (2) made substantial progress toward achieving the use.

📚 References
  • 83 Am. Jur. 2d Zoning & Planning §§ 537–44 (2019) (discussing the nature and extent of nonconforming use).

主题：不动产（Real Property）— 不动产权利（Rights in Real Property）

建筑商能否继续按其计划在2英亩地块上建造5栋房屋？

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A rancher owned in fee simple two adjoining lots, Lots 1 and 2. He conveyed Lot 1 in fee simple to his cousin. The deed was in usual form of a warranty deed with the following provision inserted in the appropriate place: "Grantor, for himself, his heirs and assigns, does covenant and agree that any reasonable expense incurred by grantee, his heirs and assigns, as the result of having to repair the retaining wall presently situated on Lot 1 at the common boundary with Lot 2, shall be reimbursed one-half the costs of repairs; and by this provision the parties intend a covenant running with the land."
The cousin conveyed Lot 1 in fee simple to a woman by warranty deed in usual and regular form. The deed omitted any reference to the retaining wall or any covenant. Fifty years after the rancher's conveyance to the cousin, the woman conveyed Lot 1 in fee simple to a developer by warranty deed in usual form. This deed omitted any reference to the retaining wall or the covenant.
There is no statute that applies to any aspect of the problems presented except a recording act and a statute providing for acquisition of title after 10 years of adverse possession. The deed from the rancher to the cousin was never recorded. All other deeds were promptly and properly recorded.
Lot 2 is now owned by the rancher's daughter, who took by intestate succession. The developer expended $3,500 on the retaining wall. Then he obtained all the original deeds in the chain of title from the rancher to himself. Shortly thereafter, the developer discovered the covenant in the rancher's deed to the cousin. The developer demanded that the daughter pay $1,750. When she refused, he instituted an appropriate action to recover that sum.
If judgment is for the daughter, what will be the likely reason?

choices.A: The cousin's deed from the rancher was never recorded.
choices.B: The developer did not know about the covenant until after he had incurred the expenses and, hence, could not have relied on it.
choices.C: The developer is barred by adverse possession.
choices.D: The developer's expenditures were not proved to be reasonable and customary.

questions.explanation:
Privity requirements for real covenants
Benefited estate
promisor
Horizontal privity
simultaneous transfer + creation of covenant
Burdened estate
promisor
Limited vertical privity
possessory interest
Vertical privity
same ownership interest
Successors in interest
Successors in interest

A real covenant is an express promise regarding land that is enforceable by an action for money damages. Although the promising parties can enforce the covenant under contract law, the covenant can bind successors in interest only if the benefit/burden runs with the land. This requires proof of the following elements:

  • Writing – covenant is in a writing that satisfies the statute of frauds (here, Lot 1 deed to the cousin)
  • Intent to run – promising parties intend for the covenant to run to their successors in interest (here, "the parties intend a covenant running with the land")
  • Touch and concern – covenant relates to the use, enjoyment, or occupation of the benefited and burdened lands (here, maintaining the shared wall)
  • Horizontal privity – promising parties simultaneously transfer the land and create the covenant (here, covenant was created when Lot 1 was deeded to the cousin)
  • Vertical privity – successor of the benefited estate has a possessory interest (here, developer owns Lot 1) and successor of the burdened estate has a promising party's entire ownership interest (here, daughter has rancher's fee simple in Lot 2)
  • Notice – if the person to be bound was a purchaser, that person had notice of the covenant (here, notice is not required because the daughter inherited Lot 2) (Choice A)

Therefore, since all requirements for binding the daughter are met, if judgment is for the daughter, the most likely reason is that the developer's expenditures were not proved to be reasonable and customary.

(Choice B) Notice is not required for successors in interest of land benefited by a real covenant (here, the developer) to enforce it.

(Choice C) Persons who acquire land subject to a real covenant through adverse possession (not seen here) cannot enforce the covenant.

📌 Educational Objective

A real covenant will bind successors in interest only if the following elements are proved: (1) writing, (2) intent to run, (3) touch and concern, (4) horizontal privity, (5) vertical privity, and (6) notice.

📚 References
  • Restatement of Property §§ 530–38 (Am. L. Inst. 1944) (discussing elements of real covenants).
questions.zh-question:
一位牧场主以完全保有地权（fee simple）拥有两个相邻地块，地块1和地块2。他将地块1的完全保有地权转让给了他的堂兄。该地契是一份常规形式的担保地契（warranty deed），并在适当位置插入了以下条款：“出让人，为其本人、其继承人和受让人，立约并同意，受让人、其继承人和受让人因必须修缮位于地块1与地块2公共边界上的现有挡土墙而产生的任何合理费用，应获偿还维修费用的一半；双方意图通过此条款设立一项随土地转移的契约（covenant running with the land）。”

堂兄通过一份常规形式的担保地契，将地块1的完全保有地权转让给了一位女士。该地契未提及挡土墙或任何契约。在牧场主转让给堂兄五十年后，该女士通过一份常规形式的担保地契将地块1的完全保有地权转让给了一位开发商。该地契也未提及挡土墙或该契约。

除了登记法案和一项规定经过10年侵权逆占（adverse possession）即可获得所有权的法规外，没有其他法规适用于本案所涉的任何方面。从牧场主到堂兄的地契从未被登记。所有其他地契都及时并妥当地进行了登记。

地块2现在由牧场主的女儿所有，她是通过无遗嘱继承（intestate succession）获得的。开发商在挡土墙上花费了3,500美元。然后，他获得了从牧场主到他自己这条所有权链中的所有原始地契。不久之后，开发商在牧场主给堂兄的地契中发现了该契约。开发商要求女儿支付1,750美元。当她拒绝后，他提起了适当的诉讼来追讨这笔款项。

如果判决有利于女儿，最可能的原因是什么？

zh-choices.A: 牧场主给堂兄的地契从未被登记。
zh-choices.B: 开发商在产生费用之后才知道该契约的存在，因此，他不可能依赖于该契约。
zh-choices.C: 开发商受到侵权逆占（adverse possession）的禁止。
zh-choices.D: 开发商的支出未被证明是合理且惯常的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Covenants & Recording Acts

核心考点：地产契约 (Real Covenant)

本题考察的是地产契约中的负担随土地转移 (Burden Running with the Land) 的条件。要让牧场主的继承人（女儿）承担付款义务，必须满足以下要素（记忆口诀 WITHN）：

  • Writing (书面形式)
  • Intent (转移意图)
  • Touch & Concern (涉及土地权益)
  • Horizontal & Vertical Privity (横向与纵向关联)
  • Notice (通知/知情)
案情梳理
地块 1 (受益方)
牧场主 (Rancher)
↓ 担保地契 (未登记)
堂兄 (Cousin)
↓
女士 (Woman)
↓
开发商 (Developer)
(原告)
地块 2 (受负方)
牧场主 (Rancher)
↓ 无遗嘱继承



女儿 (Daughter)
(被告)
⚠️ 为什么选项 A 是最大的陷阱？

选项 A 称“牧场主给堂兄的地契从未登记”。很多考生看到“未登记”就会联想到登记法案 (Recording Acts)，认为未登记导致契约无效。

关键点：登记法案只保护有偿购买者 (Purchasers for value)。本题中，女儿是通过无遗嘱继承 (Intestate Succession) 获得地块 2 的。

继承人不是购买者，不受登记法案保护。她只是站在了牧场主的位置上（step into the shoes），无论她是否知情，只要契约有效，她就必须继承该负担。

✅ 正确答案：D

“开发商的支出未被证明是合理且惯常的。”

法律推理：

  1. 契约有效且随土地转移： 所有的 WITHN 要素都满足。
    • 书面、意图、涉及土地均无争议。
    • 关联性 (Privity) 存在。
    • 通知 (Notice) 对继承人不是抗辩理由（见上文）。
  2. 回归合同条款： 既然契约对女儿有约束力，我们必须看契约的具体内容。条款明确规定："...any reasonable expense... shall be reimbursed..."（任何合理的费用……应获偿还）。
  3. 事实抗辩： 如果开发商花费了 $3,500，但无法证明这是“合理的 (reasonable)”或“惯常的 (customary)”，那么根据契约本身的条款，女儿就没有义务支付这笔钱。
🎓 MBE 考试技巧

当题目问“如果被告胜诉，理由是什么”时：

  1. 首先检查法律原则（如：契约是否随土地转移？）。
  2. 如果法律原则上被告应当承担责任（如本题中女儿无法通过Recording Act免责），那么请仔细检查事实细节或合同条款。
  3. 本题是一个典型的“法律上成立，但事实上失败”的例子。不要忽略题目中引用的具体合同措辞（"reasonable expense"）。

question_analysis.skill_tested: Identify covenant enforcement proof deficiency

label.zh: 随土地负担的约定意图

reason.en: Establishes that successors may enforce the promise as a real covenant.
reason.zh: 表明继承人可将其作为不动产约定主张执行。

keywords.text: any reasonable expense incurred by grantee

reason.en: Recovery depends on proving the costs were reasonable under the covenant.
reason.zh: 能否获偿取决于能否证明费用符合约定的合理性。

keywords.text: retaining wall presently situated on Lot 1 at the common boundary with Lot 2

reason.en: Shows the covenant touches and concerns both adjoining parcels.
reason.zh: 表明该约定涉及相邻两块土地的使用与维护。

keywords.text: The deed from the rancher to the cousin was never recorded

reason.en: Tempts a recording-act answer even though privity and notice analysis still bind the daughter.
reason.zh: 易诱使考生以登记规则作答，但相邻权义务分析仍及于女儿。

reason.en: An heir is not a purchaser, so purchaser notice rules do not block enforcement.
reason.zh: 继承人非购买者，故购买者通知规则不阻却执行。

keywords.text: omitted any reference to the retaining wall or any covenant

reason.en: Suggests merger or termination but does not defeat a covenant running with the land.
reason.zh: 看似约定已消灭，但不影响随土地负担的约定。

keywords.text: The developer expended $3,500 on the retaining wall

reason.en: Sets up whether those costs were reasonable and recoverable in the action.
reason.zh: 引出诉讼中该等费用是否合理并可请求分担。

reason.en: Misattributes defeat of the covenant to lack of record notice rather than proof of reasonableness.
reason.zh: 将败诉原因误归为未登记通知，而非费用合理性未证明。

B.text: did not know about the covenant until after he had incurred the expenses

reason.en: Implies a benefited successor must have known before spending, which is not required.
reason.zh: 暗示受益继承人须事前知情才可支出，但法律无此要求。

B.text: could not have relied on it

reason.en: Treats enforcement like a contract reliance defense for the burdened owner.
reason.zh: 将执行问题误当作对被负担方适用的合同依赖抗辩。

reason.en: Pulls in a statute mentioned in the stem though no adverse possessor appears.
reason.zh: 援引题干提及的时效取得成文法，但案情并无时效占有人。

D.text: not proved to be reasonable and customary

reason.en: Matches the covenant's reasonable-expense condition as the likely basis for judgment for the daughter.
reason.zh: 符合约定中的合理费用要件，为女儿胜诉的最可能理由。

highlights.text: any reasonable expense incurred by grantee, his heirs and assigns, as the result of having to repair the retaining wall

reason.zh: 约定仅补偿合理费用，故未证明合理性则女儿可能胜诉。

highlights.text: the parties intend a covenant running with the land

reason.en: Confirms the promise is meant to bind successors, making later privity analysis decisive.
reason.zh: 确认该承诺拟及于继承人，使后续权义务承继分析成为关键。

highlights.text: Lot 2 is now owned by the rancher's daughter, who took by intestate succession

label.zh: 负担地块的继承所有人

reason.en: Her status as heir means purchaser-notice defenses in choices A and B are unlikely winners.
reason.zh: 其继承人身份使选项A与B中的购买者通知抗辩难以成立。

highlights.text: The deed from the rancher to the cousin was never recorded

reason.en: A prominent fact that distracts from the actual proof issue on reasonable expenditures.
reason.zh: 显眼事实易分散注意力，掩盖真正争点为费用是否合理。

highlights.text: If judgment is for the daughter, what will be the likely reason?

reason.en: Frames the task as finding the operative failure despite otherwise satisfied running-with-the-land elements.
reason.zh: 要求在众多要件满足时找出实际阻却开发者获偿的理由。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A man owned a lakefront home in a gated community with a pier where he docked his boat. His neighbor, whose home did not have a pier, told him that she was interested in purchasing a boat but that she had nowhere to dock it except for the community clubhouse. The clubhouse was located at the other end of the gated community far from the neighbor's home. However, the man told the neighbor that she could use his pier to dock her boat, and as a result, the neighbor purchased a boat knowing that she could dock it close to home. For the next 11 years, the neighbor used the man's pier to dock her boat. During this time, the neighbor also paid for the pier to be rebuilt due to corrosion. Thereafter, the man told the neighbor that she could only use the pier if she paid a monthly fee of $600. When the neighbor refused to pay the fee, the man built a fence around the pier and refused to give the neighbor a key to unlock the fence.
The statutory period for acquiring rights by prescription in the jurisdiction is 10 years.
Does the neighbor have the right to use the man's pier to dock her boat?

choices.A: No, because the easement was not in a writing that satisfied the statute of frauds.
choices.B: No, because the neighbor could have docked her boat at the community clubhouse.
choices.C: Yes, because the neighbor detrimentally relied on the man's permission to use the pier.
choices.D: Yes, because the neighbor's use of the pier was continuous, actual, and open.

questions.explanation:
Distinctions between easements
Type Purpose Creation
Appurtenant
Benefits easement holder's land. Benefit & burden automatically transfer when land is conveyed.		 Affirmative
Allows easement holder to do something on servient estate.		 Express
Created by parties in writing that satisfies statute of frauds.
In gross
Benefits easement holder personally. Burden (not benefit) automatically transfers when land is conveyed.		 Negative
Restricts servient-estate owner's lawful use of servient estate.		 Irrevocable license
License becomes irrevocable due to estoppel or coupling with another servitude.
Implied
Implied by law due to necessity (easement by necessity); Implied by fact due to prior use (easement by implication).
By prescription
Adversely acquired through open/notorious, actual, continuous & nonpermissive use.

An easement is a right held by one person to make specific, limited use of land owned by another. The land subject to the easement is called the servient estate, and the land that benefits from the easement is called the dominant estate.

Although most easements are created in a writing that satisfies the statute of frauds, they can also be created by estoppel. An easement by estoppel arises from good-faith, reasonable, detrimental reliance on the servient-estate owner's permission to make a limited use of his/her land.

Here, a man (the servient-estate owner) gave his neighbor (the dominant-estate owner) permission to use his pier. The neighbor relied on this permission by purchasing a boat and paying to rebuild the pier. Thus, an easement by estoppel was created.

*An easement by estoppel can also be characterized as an irrevocable license.

(Choice A) Although an easement can be created by an express writing that satisfies the statute of frauds, it can also be created by other means, such as estoppel.

(Choice B) The fact that the neighbor could have docked her boat at the community clubhouse does not affect her right to use the pier. An easement by necessity only arises when property is rendered virtually useless—for example, when it is landlocked.

(Choice D) An easement by prescription requires hostile (nonpermissive) use. Here, the neighbor had the man's permission to use the pier, so the hostile element is missing even though her use was continuous, actual, and open for 10 years.

📌 Educational Objective

An easement by estoppel is created through good-faith, reasonable, detrimental reliance on the servient-estate owner's permission to make a limited use of his/her land.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Property: Servitudes § 2.10 (Am. Law Inst. 2000) (servitudes created by estoppel).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子在一个封闭式社区拥有一栋湖滨住宅，住宅带有一个码头，他用该码头停泊他的船。他的邻居的住宅没有码头，她告诉该男子她有兴趣购买一艘船，但除了社区会所外，她没有地方停泊。该会所位于封闭式社区的另一端，远离邻居的家。然而，该男子告诉邻居她可以使用他的码头来停泊她的船，因此，邻居在知道她可以把船停在离家近的地方后，购买了一艘船。在接下来的11年里，邻居一直使用该男子的码头停泊她的船。在此期间，邻居还因码头腐蚀而出资重建。此后，该男子告诉邻居，她只有在每月支付600美元费用的情况下才能使用该码头。当邻居拒绝支付费用时，该男子在码头周围建了一个栅栏，并拒绝给邻居打开栅栏的钥匙。

在该司法管辖区，通过时效取得权利的法定期限是10年。

邻居是否有权使用该男子的码头来停泊她的船？

zh-choices.A: 不成立，因为该地役权没有满足《防止欺诈法》(statute of frauds) 的书面形式要求。
zh-choices.B: 不成立，因为邻居本可以将其船停泊在社区会所。
zh-choices.C: 成立，因为邻居因信赖该男子的许可而使用了码头，并因此蒙受了不利。
zh-choices.D: 成立，因为邻居对码头的使用是持续的、实际的和公开的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Easements & Licenses

核心考点：禁反言地役权 Easement by Estoppel / Irrevocable License

通常情况下，许可（License）是可撤销的。但如果被许可人基于对许可的合理信赖（Reasonable Reliance），投入了大量资金或劳力（Detriment），该许可就会变为不可撤销，从而形成禁反言地役权。

案情逻辑链条
  • 许可 (Permission)：男子口头允许邻居使用码头。
  • 信赖 (Reliance)：邻居基于此许可购买了船只。
  • 投入/不利 (Detriment)：邻居不仅买了船，还出资重建了被腐蚀的码头。
  • 结果：许可变为不可撤销。

因此，正确答案是 选项 C。

陷阱选项排除
❌ 选项 A：防止欺诈法 (Statute of Frauds)

虽然地役权通常需要书面形式，但禁反言 (Estoppel) 是《防止欺诈法》的重要例外。当存在不利信赖时，无需书面文件即可成立地役权。

❌ 选项 B：必要性 (Necessity)

只有当土地完全无法使用（如“袋地” landlocked）时才适用必要地役权 (Easement by Necessity)。仅仅是因为“方便”或“不想去远处的会所”不足以构成法律上的必要性。

❌ 选项 D：时效取得 (Prescription)

这是一个经典的干扰项。虽然使用了11年（超过10年时效），但时效取得必须是敌意的 (Hostile/Adverse)。本案中邻居的使用是经过男子许可 (Permission) 的，许可直接否定了敌意，因此无法通过时效取得权利。

💡 MBE 考试技巧
当你看到题目中出现：
1. 口头允许 (Oral Permission)
2. 随后有一方投入金钱或劳力 (Investment of money/labor)

请立即联想 Irrevocable License 或 Easement by Estoppel。不要被“没有书面合同”或“时效期限”迷惑。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
The existence of an express right-of-way easement over land was discovered during a title search conducted by an individual who had contracted to buy the land. The seller desired to secure a release of the easement, so he traveled to the easement holder's neighboring property. When the seller arrived, the neighbor's adult daughter informed him that the neighbor had been living in a nursing home for the past year and that she had been taking care of his land. In exchange for a small sum, the neighbor's daughter executed the requested document. The document stated that the neighbor "hereby releases" the easement over the seller's land, which was described in full.
The seller then deeded the land to the buyer, and the neighbor died shortly thereafter. The neighbor's property passed by will to the neighbor's daughter. The daughter claims that she continues to possess a right-of-way easement over the buyer's land.
Is the neighbor's daughter correct?

choices.A: No, because the daughter signed the release of the easement.
choices.B: No, because the release was valid and terminated the easement.
choices.C: Yes, because the property interest was not a license and did not expire upon the neighbor's death.
choices.D: Yes, because the release was not signed by the neighbor and violated the statute of frauds.

questions.explanation:
Ways to terminate easements
  • Destruction – servient estate condemned or destroyed by natural forces
  • Abandonment - dominant estate abandons easement
  • Merger - dominant & servient estates united in common ownership
  • Prescription - servient owner prevents use for prescriptive period
  • Estoppel - dominant owner estopped from asserting easement
  • Release - express release in writing satisfying statute of frauds

Mnemonic: DAMPER

An easement is a nonpossessory interest in someone else's land that gives the easement holder the right to enter and use the land for a specific purpose. An easement can be terminated by a release—ie, a writing that expressly relinquishes the easement right—so long as it complies with the statute of frauds. To comply with the statute of frauds, the writing must do the following:

  • Reasonably identify the parties (the neighbor and the seller)
  • Contain words of transfer ("hereby releases")
  • Describe the nature of the easement (the easement over the seller's land was described in full)
  • Be signed by the easement holder (the neighbor)

Since the neighbor did not sign the release (the daughter did), the document secured by the seller was not a valid release that terminated the easement (Choices B & D). But since the daughter did sign the release, she will be estopped from asserting that she inherited the neighbor's right-of-way over the buyer's land.

(Choice C) Although a license typically expires upon the death of the licensee, an easement does not expire upon the death of the easement holder. This means that the neighbor's easement passed by will to his daughter. However, she will be estopped from asserting the easement's validity because she signed the release.

📌 Educational Objective

An easement can be terminated by a written release that complies with the statute of frauds. To do so, the release must (1) reasonably identify the parties, (2) contain words of transfer, (3) describe the nature of the easement, and (4) be signed by the easement holder.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Property: Servitudes § 7.3 (Am. Law Inst. 2000) (termination of an easement by release).
questions.zh-question:
在一项由土地购买合同的当事人进行的产权调查中，发现土地上存在一项明示的通行地役权。卖方希望获得该地役权的弃权书，因此他前往地役权持有人的邻近地产。当卖方到达时，邻居的成年女儿告知他，邻居在过去一年里一直住在养老院，而她一直在照管他的土地。为了换取一小笔钱，邻居的女儿签署了所要求的文件。该文件声明，邻居“在此放弃”其在卖方土地上的地役权，并对该地役权进行了完整描述。

随后，卖方将土地通过契约转让给买方，邻居不久后去世。邻居的财产通过遗嘱传给了他的女儿。女儿声称她继续拥有在买方土地上的通行地役权。

邻居的女儿是否正确？

zh-choices.A: 不正确，因为女儿签署了地役权的弃权书。
zh-choices.B: 不正确，因为弃权书有效并终止了该地役权。
zh-choices.C: 正确，因为该财产权益不是一项许可，并未因邻居的死亡而失效。
zh-choices.D: 正确，因为弃权书未经邻居本人签署，并且违反了防止欺诈法。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Easements & Estoppel
正确答案：A

不正确，因为女儿签署了地役权的弃权书 (Release)。

本题考察的是地役权的终止 (Termination of Easements) 与禁止反言 (Estoppel) 原则的交叉应用。

1. 防止欺诈法 (Statute of Frauds)

地役权 (Easement) 是土地权益。根据防止欺诈法，终止地役权的弃权书 (Release) 必须由地役权持有人 (Easement Holder) 签署才有效。

在本案中，签署弃权书时，邻居（父亲）还活着，他才是地役权持有人。女儿当时并没有所有权。因此，从技术上讲，这份弃权书在当时是无效的。

2. 禁止反言 (Estoppel)

这是本题的解题关键。虽然弃权书最初因签署人无权处分而无效，但情况发生了变化：

  • 女儿继承了土地，成为了真正的地役权持有人。
  • 女儿之前亲自签署了弃权书并接受了对价（钱）。

法律原则是：如果一个人声称放弃某项权利（即使当时她没有该权利），当她后来真正获得该权利时，她被“禁止反言” (Estopped)，即不能推翻自己之前的声明。

因此，女儿不能现在跳出来说：“嘿，我签字的时候这地不是我的，所以那个签字不算数，我现在要行使地役权。”

为什么排除其他选项？
选项 B 错误： 它声称弃权书是“有效的” (Valid)。这是不准确的法律表述。弃权书本身因违反防止欺诈法（非权利人签署）在当时是无效的。女儿无法行使权利是因为个人被禁止 (Personal Estoppel)，而不是因为文件本身完美无瑕。
选项 D 错误： 这是一个典型的“陷阱选项”。它正确地指出了弃权书违反了防止欺诈法（未由邻居签署）。但是，它忽略了禁止反言这一衡平法原则 (Equitable Doctrine)。在MBE中，如果一方的不当行为或承诺导致了不公平的结果，衡平法通常会介入。
选项 C 错误： 虽然地役权确实通常会通过遗嘱传递（不像许可 License 那样随死亡终止），但这里的关键阻碍是女儿自己的签字行为，而非继承规则。
💡 考试锦囊：DAMPER

地役权终止的六种方式

Destruction (毁损)
Abandonment (放弃)
Merger (混同)
Prescription (时效)
Estoppel (禁止反言) ✅
Release (书面弃权)

本题结合了 Release（形式要件未满足）和 Estoppel（最终结果）。

C.text: did not expire upon the neighbor's death

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A landlord orally leased a commercial building to a tenant for a 10-year term, which ended one year ago. At the beginning of the lease term, the tenant installed numerous appliances in the building as well as a large air-conditioning system. The tenant alone paid for these items; they were installed with the landlord's permission and were used for the tenant's commercial enterprise.
At the end of the lease term, the tenant failed to vacate the premises in a timely manner and continued to pay rent while remaining in possession for another four months. Before vacating the building at the end of the fourth month, the tenant removed the appliances and the air-conditioning system that he had installed, causing no damage to the building.
Was the removal by the tenant proper?

choices.A: No, because he was a holdover tenant.
choices.B: No, because the lease was oral.
choices.C: Yes, because they were accessions.
choices.D: Yes, because they were trade fixtures.

questions.explanation:
Removal of trade fixtures

10-year lease begins
Tenant installs items for his enterprise
Lease ends; tenant stays & pays rent
Tenant removes items without damage
Tenant vacates building
Tenancy for years
Periodic tenancy
Removal allowed Removal prohibited

A tenant can remove trade fixtures—items the tenant attached to real property for use in his/her trade or business—without the landlord's consent if:

  • the removal will not substantially harm the property (eg, will not degrade the building's structural integrity) and
  • the items are removed before, or within a reasonable time after, the lease terminates.

Since a periodic tenancy has no defined end date, it continues until either the landlord or tenant gives express notice to terminate it. This tenancy can be created by agreement (eg, a written lease) or by implication (eg, when the tenant continues to pay, and the landlord continues to accept, rent after a prior lease has ended).

Here, the appliances and air-conditioning system are trade fixtures since the tenant installed them for use in his commercial enterprise. And though the tenant's oral 10-year lease ended one year ago, he then initiated a periodic tenancy by continuing to use the premises and pay rent for another four months. And since the tenant removed the trade fixtures before the end of the fourth month (before the tenancy terminated) and caused no damage to the building, the removal was proper.

(Choice A) Although he was a holdover tenant—a tenant who entered a valid lease and then stayed past the end of the lease term—he became a periodic tenant when he kept possession of the premises and continued to pay rent. Therefore, he had the right to remove the trade fixtures before the periodic tenancy ended.

(Choice B) Since the 10-year lease was oral and could not be performed within a year, it was unenforceable under the statute of frauds. But the landlord and tenant then formed a periodic tenancy that (1) was not subject to the statute of frauds and (2) was still in effect when the tenant removed the trade fixtures. Therefore, the removal was proper (regardless of the prior oral lease).

(Choice C) Accessions are items that are so attached to other property that they cannot be removed without causing substantial damage. Here, the appliances and air-conditioning system were not accessions since they were removed without damaging the building. But had they been accessions, removal would have been improper.

📌 Educational Objective

Trade fixtures—items attached to real property by a tenant for use in his/her trade or business—can be removed without the landlord's consent if (1) the removal occurs before, or within a reasonable time after, the lease ends and (2) the removal will not substantially harm the property.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Prop.: Landlord & Tenant § 1.5 (Am. Law Inst. 1997) (periodic tenancy).
  • Restatement (Second) of Prop.: Landlord & Tenant §§ 12.2–12.3 (Am. Law Inst. 1997) (restoration after removal of trade fixtures).
questions.zh-question:
房东将一栋商业建筑口头出租给租户，租期为10年，该租期已于一年前结束。在租期开始时，租户在建筑物内安装了许多电器以及一个大型空调系统。这些物品由租户单独支付费用；它们是在房东的许可下安装的，并用于租户的商业企业。

在租期结束时，租户未能及时腾空房产，并继续支付租金，同时又占有了四个月。在第四个月末腾空建筑物之前，租户拆除了他安装的电器和空调系统，没有对建筑物造成任何损坏。

租户的拆除行为是否适当？

zh-choices.A: 不适当，因为他是一个逾期占用租户。
zh-choices.B: 不适当，因为租约是口头的。
zh-choices.C: 适当，因为它们是添附物。
zh-choices.D: 适当，因为它们是营业定着物。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property / Landlord & Tenant
正确答案：D

是的，因为它们是营业定着物 (Trade Fixtures)。

核心概念：营业定着物 (Trade Fixtures)

在普通法下，一般规则是附着在土地上的物品成为不动产的一部分（Fixtures），租户不得带走。但是，针对商业租赁有一个重要的例外：

  • 定义：租户为了进行商业活动（Trade or Business）而安装的设备或物品。
  • 规则：商业租户有权在租期结束前拆除这些物品。
  • 限制条件：
    1. 拆除必须发生在租期结束前（或结束后的合理时间内）；
    2. 拆除不得对房产造成实质性损害（Substantial Harm）。

在本题中，租户安装空调和电器是为了商业用途，且拆除未造成损坏，因此符合 Trade Fixtures 的定义。

难点分析：逾期占用 (Holdover Doctrine)

很多考生会困惑：“租约不是一年前就结束了吗？为什么现在还能拆？”

这里的关键在于租户的身份转变：

  • 逾期占用 (Holdover)：租期结束后，租户未搬走。
  • 周期性租赁 (Periodic Tenancy) 的形成：当逾期租户继续支付租金，且房东接受租金时，法律上这就转化为一个新的周期性租赁（通常是按月租赁）。

结论：虽然最初的10年租约结束了，但双方建立了一个新的、有效的租赁关系。租户在第四个月末搬走前拆除物品，仍然是在“当前租赁关系存续期间”进行的，因此拆除是合法的。

为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 A (Holdover Tenant):
虽然他确实曾是逾期占用者，但一旦房东接受租金，他就变成了合法的周期性租户（Periodic Tenant），拥有完整的租户权利，包括拆除营业定着物的权利。
选项 B (Oral Lease):
虽然10年口头租约违反了《反欺诈法》(Statute of Frauds)，但这与当前的拆除权无关。当前的租赁关系是基于双方行为（占有+付租）形成的周期性租赁，这是有效的。
选项 C (Accessions):
添附物 (Accessions) 通常指与不动产结合紧密、无法在不造成破坏的情况下分离的物品。如果它们是 Accessions，租户反而不能拆除。题目明确说“未造成损坏”，所以这个理由不成立。
MBE 考试技巧

遇到商业租赁 (Commercial Lease) 的题目，看到租户安装了昂贵的设备（如冷库、柜台、机器），首先反应应该是 Trade Fixtures Doctrine。

判定的核心是：Commercial Purpose（商业目的） + No Substantial Damage（无重大损害）。只要满足这两点，普通法倾向于允许租户带走这些财产。

reason.en: Misstates that holdover status alone prohibits removal, ignoring conversion to periodic tenancy.

reason.en: Shows a new periodic tenancy existed when the tenant removed the fixtures, so removal was timely.

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A man conveyed his house to his wife for life, remainder to his only child, a son by a previous marriage. Thereafter, the man died, devising his entire estate to his son.
The wife later removed a light fixture in the dining room of the house and replaced it with a chandelier that was one of her family heirlooms. She then informed her nephew and her late husband's son that after her death, the chandelier should be removed from the dining room and replaced with the former light fixture, which she had stored in the basement.
The wife died and under her will bequeathed her entire estate to her nephew. She also named the nephew as the personal representative of her estate. After the nephew, in his capacity as personal representative, removed the chandelier and replaced it with the original light fixture shortly after the wife's death, the son sued to have the chandelier reinstalled.
Who will likely prevail?

choices.A: The nephew, because he had the right to remove the chandelier within a reasonable time after the wife's death.
choices.B: The nephew, because of the doctrine of accession.
choices.C: The son, because a personal representative can remove only trade fixtures from real property.
choices.D: The son, because the chandelier could not be legally removed after the death of the wife.

questions.explanation:
Tenant annexed (ie, attached) chattel to the land
No
Cannot remove
Yes
Tenant did not intend to permanently annex chattel
No
Cannot remove
Yes
Chattel can be removed without substantial damage
No
Cannot remove
Yes
Can remove within a reasonable time

When a life tenant, the holder of a life estate, annexes (ie, attaches) a chattel to the property, the life tenant—or his/her personal representative—has the right to remove the chattel within a reasonable time after the estate ends if:

  • the life tenant did not intend for the annexation to be permanent and
  • the chattel can be removed without substantial damage to the property or the chattel.

Here, the man conveyed a life estate to his wife. She installed a chandelier (a chattel) in the home but did not intend the installation to be permanent. Accordingly, when she died and a fee simple passed to the son, the nephew, as the wife's personal representative, had the right to remove the chandelier within a reasonable time after her death.

(Choice B) The doctrine of accession does not apply here because the chandelier can be removed without substantial damage to the property or the chattel.

(Choice C) A life tenant's right to remove annexed chattel is not limited to trade fixtures (eg, store counters installed by a commercial tenant).

(Choice D) The nephew could legally remove the chandelier, which contradicts the premise of this answer choice.

📌 Educational Objective

A life tenant (or his/her personal representative) may remove an annexed chattel within a reasonable time after the life estate ends if (1) the life tenant did not intend to permanently annex the chattel and (2) its removal will not cause substantial damage.

📚 References
  • Restatement (First) of Property § 122 (Am. Law Inst. 1936) (life tenant's right to remove fixtures).
  • Restatement (Second) of Property: Landlord & Tenant § 12.2 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (tenant's rights and obligations as to physical changes to the property).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子将其房屋转让给其妻子，授予其终身保有权，剩余权益归其前次婚姻所生的独子。此后，该男子去世，并通过遗嘱将其全部遗产赠与其子。

后来，该妻子移除了房屋餐厅的一盏灯具，并换上了一件作为其家族传家宝的水晶吊灯。随后，她告知其外甥和已故丈夫的儿子，在她去世后，应将该水晶吊灯从餐厅移除，并换回她存放在地下室的原有灯具。

该妻子去世，并根据其遗嘱，将其全部遗产遗赠给其外甥。她还指定其外甥为其遗产的个人代表。在妻子去世后不久，其外甥以个人代表的身份移除了水晶吊灯并换回了原来的灯具，其后，儿子提起诉讼，要求重新安装该水晶吊灯。

谁可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 外甥，因为他有权在妻子去世后的合理时间内移除该水晶吊灯。
zh-choices.B: 外甥，因为添附原则。
zh-choices.C: 儿子，因为个人代表只能从不动产上移除营业定着物。
zh-choices.D: 儿子，因为在妻子去世后，该水晶吊灯不能被合法移除。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Fixtures
Rights in Real Property Fixtures (定着物)

本题考察的核心法律问题是：终身保有人 (Life Tenant) 是否有权移除其安装在不动产上的定着物 (Fixtures)？

⚖️ 核心法则 (The Rule) 当终身保有人将动产 (Chattel) 附着于不动产时，如果满足以下条件，该动产不成为不动产的永久部分，保有人（或其个人代表）有权将其移除：
  • 意图 (Intent)： 安装者无意将其永久赠予给剩余财产权人 (Remainderman)。
  • 损害 (Damage)： 移除不会对不动产造成实质性损害。
  • 时间 (Timing)： 必须在终身地产权终止后的合理时间内移除。

📝 案情拆解

1
安装者的身份：
妻子是终身保有人 (Life Tenant)，而非完全保有权人 (Fee Simple Owner)。法律对终身保有人移除定着物的权利通常比普通租户更宽松，因为他们知道自己的权益是暂时的。
2
主观意图 (Intent)：
妻子安装的是家族传家宝 (Heirloom)，并明确指示死后换回原灯具。这清楚地表明她没有将吊灯永久附着于房屋的意图 (No intent to annex permanently)。
3
移除行为：
外甥作为个人代表 (Personal Representative)，在妻子死后不久 (shortly after) 进行了移除。这符合“合理时间”的要求。且题目未提及移除造成了房屋损坏。
✅ 结论：外甥胜诉 (Option A)
因为他有权在合理时间内移除未被永久添附的动产。
为什么其他选项是错的？
❌ 选项 B (Doctrine of Accession):
添附原则 (Accession) 通常指动产与不动产结合得如此紧密，以至于无法分离，从而导致动产所有权转移给不动产所有人。本案中吊灯可以被移除且无损毁，因此不适用该原则。如果适用，胜诉的应该是儿子（不动产所有人）。
❌ 选项 C (Trade Fixtures Only):
这是一个常见的干扰项。虽然“营业定着物” (Trade Fixtures) 确实允许商业租户移除，但终身保有人移除定着物的权利不限于商业用途。家庭装饰类定着物 (Domestic fixtures) 只要符合意图测试，同样可以移除。
❌ 选项 D (Cannot be removed after death):
法律允许终身保有人的个人代表在终身权益终止后的一段合理时间 (Reasonable Time) 内进入房产移除定着物。权利并不会在死亡瞬间立即消失。
MBE Tips: 在定着物问题中，安装者的“意图”通常是决定性因素，尤其是当安装者是租户或终身保有人时。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
An architect and a developer own adjacent parcels of land. On each of their parcels was a low-rise office building. The two office buildings were of the same height.
Last year the developer decided to demolish the low-rise office building on her parcel and to erect a new high-rise office building of substantially greater height on her parcel as permitted by the zoning and building ordinances. She secured all the governmental approvals necessary to pursue her project.
As the developer's new building was in the course of construction, the architect realized that the shadows it would create would place the architect's building in such deep shade that the rent she could charge for space in her building would be substantially reduced.
The architect brought an appropriate action against the developer to enjoin the construction in order to eliminate the shadow problem and for damages. The architect presented uncontroverted evidence that her evaluation as to the impact of the shadow on the fair rental value of her building was correct. There is no statute or ordinance (other than the building and zoning ordinances) that is applicable to the issues before the court.
How should the court rule?

choices.A: Award the architect damages measured by the loss of rental value, but not an injunction.
choices.B: Grant judgment for the developer, because she had secured all the necessary governmental approvals for the new building.
choices.C: Grant judgment for the developer, because the architect has no legal right to have sunshine continue to reach the windows of her building.
choices.D: Grant the architect the requested injunction.

questions.explanation:
Remedies for nuisance & easement actions

Temporary nuisance Permanent nuisance Misuse / interference of easement
Damages
  • Diminished rental value
  • Reasonable repair costs
  • Incidental loss
  • Loss of use & enjoyment
  • Punitive damages
  • Diminished land value
  • Rents received
  • Decreased value of servient estate and/or easement
  • Value of excessive use
  • Cost of restoration
  • Loss of use
Injunction Available N/A Available
Self-help Available N/A Available
Forfeiture N/A Unavailable unless injunction will not relieve servient estate

The Doctrine of Ancient Lights, which originated in England and provides that a landowner acquires an easement for light and air after 20 years of uninterrupted access, has been rejected in the United States. Blockage of light is generally not a public or private nuisance unless motivated by malice. A right to light exists only if it is protected by statute or by an express negative easement.

Applied to these facts, the court should grant judgment for the developer because the architect has no legal right to light. (Choices A & D)

(Choice B) Governmental approvals do not bar others from exercising their legal rights, but because no right to light exists here, this fact is irrelevant.

📌 Educational Objective

A landowner only has a right to light if (1) this right is protected by statute or (2) the landowner enters into an express agreement with the other landowner to create a negative easement or covenant.

📚 References
  • Mohr v. Midas Realty Corp., 431 N.W.2d 380, 382 (Iowa 1988)
  • Sher v. Leiderman, 226 Cal. Rptr. 698, 701 (Ct. App. 1986)
questions.zh-question:
一位建筑师和一位开发商拥有相邻的地块。在他们各自的地块上，都有一座低层办公楼。这两座办公楼高度相同。

去年，开发商决定拆除其地块上的低层办公楼，并根据分区和建筑条例的许可，在其地块上建造一座高度显著增加的新高层办公楼。她获得了推进其项目所需的所有政府批准。

当开发商的新建筑正在施工时，建筑师意识到其产生的阴影将使她的建筑处于极深的阴影中，从而导致她可以收取的建筑空间租金大幅下降。

建筑师对开发商提起了适当的诉讼，要求禁止施工以消除阴影问题，并要求损害赔偿。建筑师出示了无可争议的证据，证明她对阴影影响其建筑公平租赁价值的评估是正确的。除了建筑和分区条例之外，没有其他法规或条例适用于法院审理的这些问题。

法院应如何裁决？

zh-choices.A: 判给建筑师以租金价值损失计算的损害赔偿，但不发布禁令。
zh-choices.B: 作出对开发商有利的判决，因为她已获得新建筑所需的所有政府批准。
zh-choices.C: 作出对开发商有利的判决，因为建筑师没有法律权利要求阳光持续照射到其建筑的窗户。
zh-choices.D: 准予建筑师所请求的禁令。

questions.zh-explanation:
核心考点：采光权
Rights to Light and Air

本题考察的是美国不动产法中关于相邻土地所有者是否有权要求获得阳光照射（即采光权）的经典规则。

1. 法律原则解析

一般规则：
在美国，土地所有者没有获得阳光、空气或景观穿过邻居土地的自然权利。

这与英国普通法中的“古老采光权原则” (Doctrine of Ancient Lights) 截然不同。在美国，法院普遍拒绝承认通过时效取得采光地役权 (Prescriptive Easement for Light)。

这意味着，只要邻居的建设行为符合当地的分区条例 (Zoning Ordinances)，且不是出于纯粹的恶意，他们就有权在自己的土地上进行建设，即使这会挡住你的阳光。

2. 案情分析与正确答案

正确答案是 C。

推理逻辑：

  • 现状：开发商 (Developer) 正在合法建造高层建筑。
  • 后果：新建筑的阴影损害了建筑师 (Architect) 的租金收益。
  • 关键点：题目明确指出没有相关的法规保护采光，双方也没有签订协议。

因此，建筑师没有法律依据 (Legal Right) 要求阳光持续照射其窗户。既然没有权利被侵犯，法院就不会判给损害赔偿 (Damages)，也不会发布禁令 (Injunction)。

3. 为什么其他选项是错的？

❌ 选项 A (判赔偿但不禁令)：
只有在存在法律上的侵权行为 (Tort) 或违约行为时，才会有损害赔偿。既然开发商有权建造，建筑师的损失属于“无损之伤” (Damnum Absque Injuria)——即虽然有经济损失，但法律不予救济。

❌ 选项 B (因为获得了政府批准)：
这是一个常见的干扰项。虽然开发商获得了批准是一个有利事实，但它不是开发商胜诉的根本法律原因。如果建筑师拥有有效的“消极地役权” (Negative Easement)，即使开发商有政府批准，建筑师依然可以胜诉。开发商胜诉的根本原因是建筑师本身缺乏采光权。

❌ 选项 D (发布禁令)：
同选项 A，没有权利受损，就没有救济措施。

4. MBE 考试通关秘籍

在处理此类“邻里纠纷”题目时，请按以下步骤思考：

  1. 看合同：是否有书面的消极地役权 (Negative Easement) 或限制性契约 (Restrictive Covenant) 禁止遮挡阳光？
  2. 看恶意：是否构成“恶意围栏” (Spite Fence)？即邻居建造该结构的唯一目的是为了伤害他人，而无任何使用价值。（本题中开发商是为了商业利益，故不构成恶意）。
  3. 看妨害：单纯的阻挡光线通常不构成私人妨害 (Private Nuisance)。
结论：如果没有合同，也没有恶意，在美国法下，你通常无权阻止邻居建楼挡光。
MBE Property Law Review | Q86196
